title: The foreknown notary has not committed a night since 2026-09-03 -- practice/export.py's continuity figure summed catches as a count, and darkocean/continuity/2026-09-03.json was the first night that count was ever nonzero
statement: No `foreknown: notary run of <date>` commit exists for 2026-09-04 or 2026-09-05, and no directory for either date exists under foreknown/snapshots/ or foreknown/reaction/snapshots/ -- the register's newest committed night is still 2026-09-03 (foreknown/snapshots/2026-09-03/, committed by a52de8a). darkocean/readings and memoryhole/readings, produced by separate workflows (darkocean.yml, memoryhole.yml) that do not call practice.export, both continued on schedule through 2026-09-04 with no gap. `practice/src/practice/export.py`'s `figures()` (pre-repair, line 93) computed the continuity-divergence figure as `sum(int(probe.get("catches") or 0) for probe in probes)` over every darkocean/continuity/<date>.json. `catches` in that file is an array of catch objects -- darkocean/continuity.py's own output shape, unchanged since the register was built -- never a count. Every continuity probe from 2026-08-11.json through 2026-09-02.json (24 files) carries `catches: []`; an empty list is falsy, so `[] or 0` evaluates to `0` and `int(0)` never raised. darkocean/continuity/2026-09-03.json (obs-2026-09-05-1.json's own subject: the register's first-ever gone_from_catalog catch) is the first file where `catches` holds anything -- 4 entries -- and a non-empty list is truthy, so `probe.get("catches") or 0` returns the list itself and `int([...])` raises `TypeError: int() argument must be a string, a bytes-like object or a real number, not 'list'`. darkocean/continuity/2026-09-04.json carries the identical 4 catches (same 4 product ids, still `"current": null`), so the same crash recurs on every subsequent night this figure is computed, not just the first. `.github/workflows/sentinel.yml`'s own committed comment (added the same night as obs-2026-09-05-1.json, before this defect was traced to its root) already names the outward symptom -- "python -m practice.export raised on 2026-09-04 and 2026-09-05" -- and repairs the workflow so that failure can no longer take a notarized night's commit down with it (`if: always()` on the export, moments and verify steps; commit gated on verify's own outcome, not export's). That repair had not yet been exercised by a scheduled run as of this pass: both visible sentinel failures (the runs that checked out 7fa8327 and 33ab9c7) ran before the `if: always()` fix landed on main, so both still show the old, fully-gated behaviour -- export fails, moments still runs, and nothing after it (verify, commit) appears in either job's log at all. The `if: always()` fix repairs the symptom (a broken mirror step can no longer discard a notarized night); it does not touch `figures()` itself, so `export.json` would keep failing to regenerate, silently, every night this figure is computed, for as long as any committed continuity probe holds a catch -- which, once darkocean/continuity/2026-09-03.json existed, is every night from here on.
method: Ran `git log --oneline --grep="notary run"` and listed foreknown/snapshots/ and foreknown/reaction/snapshots/ to confirm the newest committed night is 2026-09-03, with no directory or commit for 2026-09-04 or 2026-09-05. Read every darkocean/continuity/2026-08-*.json and .../2026-09-*.json with python3/json.load and printed `len(catches)` per file to establish the 24-night run of empty lists, the first nonzero file (2026-09-03, 4 catches), and its continuation into 2026-09-04.json (the same 4 product ids, still absent). Read practice/src/practice/export.py's `figures()` in full and confirmed by inspection that `probe.get("catches")` is compared against `0` and passed to `int()`, while every continuity probe file types `catches` as a JSON array. Reproduced the exact crash locally: `python3 -m practice.export --repo-root .` against the committed working tree raised `TypeError: int() argument must be a string, a bytes-like object or a real number, not 'list'` at export.py line 93, the same exception named (without traceback detail) in sentinel.yml's own comment. Cross-checked the failure's history and exact traceback against GitHub's own Actions run logs for the sentinel workflow (runs that checked out 7fa8327 and 33ab9c7, both completed with conclusion "failure", both showing this identical traceback at the identical line) -- corroboration for the timeline, not a substitute for the committed evidence above, which is sufficient on its own to prove and fix the defect. Repaired export.py to count catches by length (`sum(len(probe.get("catches") or []) for probe in probes)`), matching how `rechecks` already correctly reads `answered` as the count field it actually is. Added practice/tests/test_export.py: one case asserting the figure stays 0 across every-file-empty probes (the 24-night baseline), one asserting a nonzero `catches` list is counted by length instead of raising. Ran `python3 -m practice.export --repo-root .` again post-repair: it completes and writes export.json without error (reverted afterward -- regenerating export.json is the sentinel workflow's own job, not discovery's, and committing a copy stamped with this session's HEAD would misstate `generated_from.commit`). Ran the full suite (171 passed, up from 169) and `verify.py` (verify.py does not read export.json or figures() at all, so this repair is orthogonal to the provenance chain it checks).
worth_watching_because: This is a fourth, mechanically distinct cause of the exact outward symptom sensor-registry-stall.json has tracked since 2026-08-11 (a register silently behind, no autonomy/log.jsonl trace for the failed step, no source-outage record) -- and, unlike the three causes that sensor's review history already lists (a verify-step deadlock, a git push race, a resolution-status logic contradiction), this one was never actually gated on the commit at all: sentinel.yml's own comment already named and repaired the *gating* failure (export's crash taking the whole night down with it) without ever tracing *why* export crashes, so the underlying defect was still live and still uncorrected on main going into this pass. It is also a direct, mechanical consequence of obs-2026-09-05-1.json's own finding two nights ago: fixing one blind spot (verify.py never checking gone_from_catalog catches) is what let the register's first real catch stand un-contradicted -- and that same first real catch is what exposed a second, unrelated blind spot (export.py's count-vs-list confusion) that 24 nights of all-empty data had never exercised. Whether tonight's repair is enough to let sentinel's next scheduled run reach a commit cannot be confirmed from the committed record alone -- that run had not yet fired as of this pass -- so sensor-registry-stall.json's own open question (does a stall self-correct once its cause is fixed, or does it take a repair landing mid-gap to end it) gets a concrete near-term test: if the notary resumes on its next run without another manual intervention, that is the first clean instance the sensor's firing-rule question has ever had.
left_alone: Not writing a new sensor-<slug>.json for this: the repair closes a genuine bug in an existing, already-admitted export path (practice.export, admitted 2026-08-09 per its own module docstring reference to attention-export/1) rather than adding a new nightly indicator, matching the same repair-not-proposal call obs-2026-09-05-1.json made for verify.py's parallel gap. Not adding a review entry to sensor-registry-stall.json's own history: that sensor's test_rule and firing-rule question are about *whether a nightly job's commit happens at all*, and tonight's finding is about a defect that (after sentinel.yml's own same-night fix) no longer gates the commit -- it belongs in that sensor's future review once a post-repair notary run either does or doesn't land, not as a repair note today. Not committing the regenerated export.json produced while verifying the fix locally -- that file's `generated_from.commit` field is only meaningful when written by the workflow that actually notarizes a night, and this pass notarizes nothing. Not asserting whether the four gone_from_catalog products will ever reappear, or extending obs-2026-09-05-1.json's own claim about them -- unchanged since that observation, still absent, still not this pass's to interpret. Not touching darkocean/continuity.py or verify.py's check_darkocean_continuity, both already correct and already covered by practice/tests/test_darkocean.py and test_verify_darkocean_gone_from_catalog.py. No memoryhole/verdicts file: memoryhole/readings/2026-09-04.json, the newest reading, carries zero rule-layer abstentions across all 20 entries.
